- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.67) and recent prices are rising — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (e.g., <0.33) — model fails to account for downward pressure.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes; correct by reducing forecast peak values by 5–10% after a spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show strong upward momentum, forecast should gradually taper downward.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile, model overfits short-term noise — apply smoothing or reduce volatility weight in forecast.
- Forecast horizon 30d often overestimates early in the period (first 5–7 days) — adjust downward by 2–5% for first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment turns negative after a spike, model fails to correct — add a downward bias of 3–5% for the next 3–5 days.
